Option

Lay out the live options for a next move side by side, each with what to do, its cost in time, and what it does for head, heart and wallet, with the leading option marked.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1CardSurface card; the leading option carries a cyan border (cyan means the action)surface, cyan
2IdMono caps (Option A, Option B · leads)text-secondary, cyan when leading
3NameHeadline step--fs-headline
4CostTime it takes, mono, right aligned from a 38rem containertext-secondary
5DoWhat the option does, one sentencetext
6Head, heart, walletA dl of three cells: the reasoning, the relationship, the moneyelevated

Usage

Use it when

  • Two to four live options for one decision, each costed.
  • The reader picks; the page does not decide for them.

Do not use it when

  • Do not mark more than one option as leading.
  • Do not use green for the leading option: green means proven, and an option is a bet.
  • Do not add an option that nobody would pick; dead options dilute the choice.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
options[]{id, name, cost, do, head, heart, wallet, lead?}yeslead: true on at most one option.

Access

  • Each option is a block in source order; the id says which leads in words (Option B · leads).
  • Head, heart and wallet are a definition list, so a screen reader pairs each label with its value.
